decisions: Commit fully to the Enterprise Autonomous Orchestrator as our next major product bet.
Execute a 6-week, constrained pilot with 2-3 enterprise design partners to validate target buyer hypotheses (CIO vs. VP of R&D).
Develop the 'Asynchronous Command Center' UX to build enterprise trust through steerability and human-in-the-loop approval gates.
Concede the consumer PR news cycle for the next two quarters, restricting all go-to-market and brand education to B2B channels.
Ring-fence a dedicated compute cluster explicitly carved out of the Q3 R&D allocation buffer.
Deploy manual, bespoke flat-rate contracts for the 2-3 pilot design partners to bypass current billing limitations.
Strictly cap the pilot at a maximum of 3 partners.

disagreements.topic: The initial target enterprise buyer wedge: CIO (cost displacement) vs. VP of R&D (time-to-discovery).
disagreements.resolution: unresolved; deferred to execution phase by sourcing partners from both segments to empirically test willingness-to-pay during the 6-week pilot.

disagreements.topic: Feasibility of a variable-compute, consumption-based pricing model for the initial pilot.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved via compromise; COO bypassed the billing engine entirely for the pilot, mandating 'bespoke, flat-rate manual contracts' while emitting raw compute logs to discover unit economics post-pilot.
